svg.aria-label: Diagram: Step Functions workflows exposed to AI agents as MCP tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. AWS states that the agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, while Step Functions runs each step exactly as defined, so the determinism the launch provides applies inside the workflow rather than to the decision to invoke it. The three workflow types carry three different execution guarantees and all three are reachable by an agent. Standard workflows are exactly-once and automatically return an idempotent response on starting an execution with the same name as a currently-running workflow, which makes the execution name the idempotency key. Asynchronous Express workflows are at-least-once and idempotency is not automatically managed, so starting multiple workflows with the same name results in concurrent executions. Synchronous Express workflows are at-most-once and idempotency is not automatically managed. Standard workflows run up to one year and their full execution history can be retrieved for up to 90 days, while Express workflows run up to five minutes and their execution history is not captured by Step Functions unless logging is enabled through Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
svg.title: The order is guaranteed; the number of times is not
svg.text: The determinism is inside the workflow.
Step Functions as an MCP tool — what the launch guarantees, and what it hands to a model.
THE AGENT DECIDES
“Your agent decides when to run a workflow
and what input to pass”
Non-deterministic caller. May retry on an
ambiguous result.
STEP FUNCTIONS DECIDES
“Step Functions runs each step exactly
as you defined it”
Order, retries, branching — settled in review,
by people, in a readable state machine.
“run multi-step business processes in the same order every time” — order, not frequency.
All three execution models are now reachable by an agent, and they do not behave alike
STANDARD — “Exactly-once workflow execution”
“Automatically returns an idempotent response on starting an execution with the same name as a
currently-running workflow” — so the execution name is the idempotency key.
EXPRESS, ASYNCHRONOUS — “At-least-once workflow execution”
“Idempotency is not automatically managed. Starting multiple workflows with the same name results in
concurrent executions.” — a retried tool call is a second run.
EXPRESS, SYNCHRONOUS — “At-most-once workflow execution”, idempotency not managed.
Duration
Standard: “up to one year”
Express: “can run for up to five minutes”
A tool call is a conversational turn. A year is not.
The record of what the agent did
Standard: full history “for up to 90 days”
Express: “not captured by Step Functions”
“Logging must be enabled through CloudWatch Logs.”
Derive the execution name from the business operation, not per call.
That is the one wiring choice that decides whether exactly-once protects the thing you care about, and it is
made outside the workflow.
Workflow type cannot be changed after creation, so the execution guarantee is chosen once, up front.
